item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=adverse+effects+of+operational+constraints+on+system+utility+in+logistics+and+transportation+AI&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1016/j.tre.2026.105012\", \"title\": [\"Hybrid quantum AI in logistics and operations management: Operational fit and strategic value\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tre.2026.105012\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 10]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7117251\", \"title\": [\"Shared Responsibility under Implementation Constraints: Governance and Operational Asymmetries in Brazil’s Medicine Reverse Logistics System\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Formally regulated reverse logistics systems are often assumed to improve post-consumer waste management once legal responsibilities, targets, and reporting mechanisms are established. However, its implementation remain uneven when regulatory design is not matched by operational capacity, territorial accessibility, reliable data, and realistic circularity outcomes. This article examines this issue through the Brazilian reverse logistics system for household medicine waste. Drawing on documentary analysis of legal frameworks and LogMed/SINIR implementation reports for 2021–2023, combined with eleven semi-structured interviews with pharmacies, pharmaceutical manufactures, and a sectoral entity, the study investigates how shared responsibility shapes implementation in practice. The findings show that the system expanded in the municipalities covered, the number of collection points, and the collected volume, but expansion did not achieve full infrastructure density or balanced implementation. Pharmacies and drugstores operate as frontline nodes and bear significant operational burdens, including space constraints, consumer disposal errors, segregation requirements, and limitations on collection frequency. Collective governance arrangements provide scale, standardization, and coordination, yet also create distance between financing actors and daily operations. Monitoring remains constrained by fragmented information systems, limited traceability, and unresolved questions of data legitimacy.
